q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of one kilometre of bitumen road?
title: Bitumen road carbon footprint per km
short: Work out the tonnes of mix laid from width, length, thickness and density. Add the mixing plant fuel, the paver and roller diesel and the haulage diesel at 2.68 kg CO2 per litre. Then add bitumen and aggregate from supplier or named database factors.
audience: Road contractors, highway developers and project consultants

ul: Hot mix: plant burner fuel and plant electricity.
Bitumen and aggregate, from supplier data.
Earthwork and base layers, if in scope.

p: Use the measurement book or bill of quantities for the layers laid, and the plant's fuel log per tonne of mix. State the density you use.
Plant and equipment the contractor owns are its Scope 1. Hired tippers and bought mix sit in Scope 3. A client that reports emissions counts the road in its Scope 3 capital goods.

example.title: Worked example: one km of 50 mm wearing course (illustrative inputs)
lines: Asphalt laid: 7 m wide x 1,000 m x 0.05 m x 2.4 t per m3 = 840 t
Mixing plant burner diesel: 840 t x 7 litres = 5,880 litres x 2.68 = 15,758.4 kg CO2
Paver and rollers: 600 litres x 2.68 = 1,608 kg CO2
Tipper haulage: 2,500 litres x 2.68 = 6,700 kg CO2
Energy total per km: 24,066.4 kg CO2, before bitumen and aggregate from supplier data
example.note: Fuel rates, thickness and density are illustrative; use the plant fuel log and the measurement book.

senseible: Senseible reads diesel invoices, fuel slips and site electricity bills into a dated, fingerprinted record per project, so a contractor can hand a client Scope 1 and 2 figures with the document behind each line. Estimates from hours or distance are labelled as estimates.
